# Instagram Post Metrics Reporting

Collect metrics from recent Instagram posts and deliver a verified spreadsheet.
Use this when the user wants the latest N posts from a profile summarized in Excel,
especially for professional/business accounts where post-level insights are visible on web.

## When to Use

- The user asks for a spreadsheet of the latest Instagram posts.
- The task is to capture post metrics from a professional account and organize them.
- The output must land in `Downloads` or another user-facing folder and be verified.
- When the account is vault-managed (institutional accounts in a curated vault), the deliverable is the vault's **canonical base**, not a loose spreadsheet in `Downloads` — see the `acirv-notebook-vault` skill.

## Prerequisites

- The user is already authenticated in Instagram Web.
- The target account is accessible from the current session.
- If insights require a professional/business login or a permission wall appears, stop and ask the user to authenticate instead of guessing credentials.
- For `.xlsx` output, use Python + `openpyxl`.

## Two Layers - Capture Both

Instagram exposes two different layers, and they do **not** reconcile by summing:

| | Camada 1 — post a post | Camada 2 — painel da conta |
|---|---|---|
| Onde | `/<tipo>/<shortcode>/` ou `/insights/media/<media_id>/` | `/accounts/insights/?timeframe=30` |
| Unidade | o post, pelo `media_id` | a conta, no período |
| Escopo | feed + reels do grid | tudo: Posts, Reels, **Stories**, Vídeos, e o split Instagram/Facebook |
| Como conta | visualizações **acumuladas** do post até a coleta | visualizações **ocorridas** na janela, em todo o conteúdo (inclusive de meses anteriores) |
| Saída | base canônica por post | foto do painel (totais, %, listas de destaque) |

The account panel is always larger - in a verified month it reported ~1,3M views over 30 days against
~500k summed from that period's posts (2,6x), because it adds Stories (~31% of its total), Facebook
cross-posts, the rolling-window effect, and views on content published before the period. **Never
present the two as the same number, and never "fix" one to match the other.**

Capture **both** layers every time. The per-post base answers "how did each post perform"; the panel
answers "how did the account perform in the window" - and it is the number the user sees in the app,
so a report with only one of them always provokes the question of why they differ.

**Stories are a third measurement, not part of either layer.** They have no likes/comments and no row in
the per-post base, and their views are not a slice of the base total either. When the ask covers stories
(quantity per month/day, what each story showed, its insight panel), keep them in their own capture and
follow `references/archived-stories-capture.md`.

## Core Workflow

1. **Confirm access first**
   - Open Instagram Web and verify you can reach the target profile.
   - Confirm the account is the intended one before collecting data.

2. **Find the complete owned-post set**
   - Prefer direct profile navigation.
   - Identify post URLs from links containing `/p/` or `/reel/` on the profile page.
   - When the request covers a whole year, date range, or says “all posts”, repeatedly force a downward scroll on the profile grid/feed so Instagram has time to lazy-load older posts. Continue persistent scrolling until several consecutive scrolls add no new owned-post URLs, or until posts clearly pass the requested start date.
   - After each scroll batch, harvest and deduplicate the newly loaded URLs; do not rely only on the first viewport.
   - Filter by the requested date range and verify chronological coverage before opening posts. Do not stop at “some recent posts”.

3. **Open each post directly**
   - Navigate to the post URL itself.
   - Once loaded, inspect both the visible page text and DOM-extracted text.

4. **Prefer text extraction over brittle clicking**
   - If `browser_snapshot` is sparse or misses rendered content, use `browser_console` to read `document.body.innerText` and relevant metadata.
   - On some Instagram post pages, the insight metrics are already present in the inline rendered text even when clicking **Ver insights** fails.
   - Before retrying clicks, inspect the current text; do not assume the metric is unavailable just because the snapshot is empty.

5. **Normalize metrics carefully**
   - Capture the post identity: URL, shortcode, publication time text, timestamp when available, caption snippet.
   - Capture every visible metric with its label, not just headline totals.
   - Preserve raw extracted lines in addition to normalized columns so later review can reconcile ambiguities.
   - Prefer explicitly labeled insight values over public social proof text like “Curtido por X e outras Y pessoas”.

6. **Build the workbook**
   - Create at least these sheets:
     - `Resumo`: one row per post with normalized fields.
     - `RawInsights`: raw label/value lines for auditability.
     - `Observacoes`: collection notes, caveats, timestamp, and source profile.
   - Keep the sheet human-readable: bold header row, freeze panes, autofilter, wrapped text for captions/notes.

7. **Verify the artifact**
   - Re-open the workbook with `openpyxl.load_workbook`.
   - Confirm the file exists, sheet names are correct, and row counts are plausible.
   - Only then tell the user it is ready.

8. **Capture the account-level panel (camada 2)**
   - Read `/accounts/insights/?timeframe=30` (also `7`, `14`, `90`) and record, with the read's date/time:
     `Visualizações` (with the Instagram/Facebook split), `Visualizadores`, `Interações`, `Contas com
     engajamento`, `Atividade do perfil` (visitas + toques em links), `Total de seguidores`, and the
     content-type split.
   - Read the ranked content lists:
     `/accounts/insights/content/?media_type=all&metric=views&sort_by=highest&timeframe=30&view_type=card`,
     then the same with `metric=interactions` and `media_type=posts|reels|stories|videos`.
   - Store the panel snapshot as its own file (`_painel_conta_<YYYY-MM-DD>_<timeframe>.json`) beside the
     captures - never inside the per-post base. Run `scripts/coletar_painel_conta.js` in the page for both
     blocks (overview + ranked list) instead of hand-writing the DOM walk; `references/account-level-insights-panel.md`
     holds the full recipe, the DOM layout and the reconciliation arithmetic.

9. **Report both layers, with the reconciliation spelled out**
   - Give the per-post totals for the period and the panel totals for its window side by side, and state
     in one line why they differ (janela, Stories/Facebook, visualizacao por data, unicidade). A bare
     panel number next to a bare base number reads as a contradiction to the user.

## Recommended Extraction Pattern

When Instagram’s structured snapshot is too thin, extract with browser JS:

- `document.body.innerText` for visible metrics and labels.
- `meta[property="og:description"]` / `og:title` for post summary text.
- `time` element for machine-readable post datetime when present.
- Link harvesting from the profile page to enumerate recent posts.

## Pitfalls

- **Sparse snapshots are not proof of missing data.** Instagram often renders useful text that the accessibility snapshot omits.
- **“Ver insights” may fail to click even when insights are already visible inline.** Inspect page text before retrying.
- **Metric labels vary slightly.** Preserve raw labels and map them conservatively instead of forcing guesses.
- **The profile grid can look complete while hiding everything.** The grid appends older items **only when the page is scrolled to its actual bottom** (`window.scrollTo(0, document.body.scrollHeight)` + ~1.5 s wait, repeated until `scrollHeight` stops growing). Small-step scrolling (250-700 px) leaves the page stuck at ~24 items and silently truncates the enumeration — that, not DOM virtualization, was the real cause of the apparent gaps. Scroll in batches of 3-4 bottom-jumps per call, harvest + dedupe after each, and stop once you pass the first post outside the requested period.
- **`og:description` dates are upload/scheduling dates, not publication dates.** A batch created on 23-28/ago published on 01-08/set looked like "missing August posts" and cost hours. Always date posts from the rendered `<time datetime>` (absolute dates for posts >7 days old also appear in the page text). See `references/pitfalls-datas-autoria-grid.md` for this plus the authorship test ("Ver insights" present = owned/co-authored; absent = third party merely tagging), date bracketing by grid position, and the fact that `openpyxl` is only reachable via `terminal`.
- **The panel's top line `Curtidas <n>` carries the COMMENT count, not likes.** On reels and many feed posts the header renders a single value under the label "Curtidas" whose number equals the post's comments (e.g. header `Curtidas 128` while the labeled block says `Curtidas 7.842` / `Comentários 128`). Never take `curtidas` from the header — always read it from the labeled breakdown block (`Interações com posts` / `Interações com reels` → `Curtidas`). Carousel/feed panels sometimes render two bare numbers (`77\n4`) which *are* likes/comments; treat only that form as a likes header.
- **The trailing `Facebook` sub-section silently overwrites real numbers.** Under `Perfil` the panel repeats `Visualizações`, `Reações` and `Comentários` with the *Facebook* cross-post numbers (tiny values). Parsing the whole text lets those clobber the Instagram values — one reel with 115.839 views and 128 comments was read as 252 views / 0 comments, and the month's view total came out 207.424 instead of 445.217. Truncate the text at the first `\nFacebook\n` before parsing.
- **`--`, `9+`, and `NN%` values are not metrics.** The panel emits `--` for hidden profile activity, `9+` as a "more metrics" placeholder (it also appears trailing, after a `Seguidores` label), and percentages for follower splits. Drop any of these from integer columns and record them as absent, otherwise `novos_seguidores` ends up as the string `96.2%`.
- **Persist every capture to disk as you go, never only in the chat.** Four posts were re-read successfully in conversation but their values were never written to a file, so the whole month had to be re-fetched. Write each batch to `_raw_bNN.jsonl` immediately; when re-reading, keep the longest capture per `media_id` (a complete re-read should win over a collapsed one).
- **Resume the previous run instead of restarting the month.** A month is collected across several sittings; the consolidated workbook often survives in the vault while the raw per-post files do not. Read the covered window from the consolidation before touching the browser, and when the prior working directory is not on disk, **ask the user where it is** — recreating the directory or re-implementing the pipeline silently re-collects already-parsed posts and duplicates the report. See `references/insights-collection-playbook.md`.
- **A previous run's grid inventory is a snapshot, never an extendable base.** `_grid_inventario.json` records the grid as it stood at capture time (`cobertura_grid: [newest, oldest]`) and nothing newer can be derived from it, so collecting the *remaining* part of a period always needs a fresh top-down grid sweep down to the old boundary. Verify a claimed working directory by searching *inside* its path — a directory-**name** glob returns zero matches even when the folder exists, which reads as "missing" and wastes a round-trip with the user.
- **A follow-up run over the rest of a period is a copy of the pipeline, not an overwrite.** Copy the scripts to suffixed siblings and rewrite artifact names programmatically, asserting every expected token was found before writing (a silent no-op substitution re-reads the previous run's inputs and ships a report of the wrong window). Point the output at a **new** filename, adapt the validator's hardcoded counts and owned/collab split to the new window, and make the builder read the new window's worklist — filtering the full-period inventory selects posts this run never captured and fires its own completeness assertion. See `references/incremental-run-and-pipeline-copies.md`.
- **A fresh sweep earns trust by agreeing with the previous run on the overlap.** Shared positions must match media_id for media_id; a divergence means the shortcode → media_id/date derivation is wrong, not that the data moved. Collaborator posts carry a longer token — slice to the leading 11 characters before decoding.
- **Diff the grid inventory against the worklist before declaring a period closed.** A sweep can store a position with a *concatenated* token (the shortcode glued to the following id, e.g. `DdFXhdwp0L9-io7p…`), and any builder that filters the grid by that broken token drops the post silently — the period then looks complete one item short. Reconcile grid items → worklist → captured records by `media_id` (not by count), and capture the missing position explicitly instead of trusting the total.
- **The per-post panel renders standalone at `/insights/media/<media_id>/`.** No click on "Ver insights" is needed. Poll for the panel's own label (`Visualiza`) plus a length floor instead of sleeping and hoping; a page that is still mounting returns a short body that looks like missing data.
- **A `--` that survives a re-read is genuinely absent.** When a panel looks partial (`Interações --`, `Contas Meta alcançadas --`), wait a few seconds and read once more: a value that fills in was mid-render, a value that stays `--` is missing data (usual on collaborator posts) — record the absence and stop re-fetching that post.
- **When a whole panel is `--`, fall back to the public media endpoint instead of retrying forever.** A post owned by a third party where the account is only a co-author exposes no insights at all (`Visualizações --`, `Visualizadores --`, `Interações --`). Read the public media info (`/api/v1/media/<media_id>/info/` with the web `x-ig-app-id` header) for `play_count` / `like_count` / `comment_count`, plus `coauthors` to prove the account really is a co-author, and file those numbers as an explicitly labelled fallback — never as panel truth. Burn one control post that reads normally to prove the wall is post-specific and not rate limiting or a lost login.
- **Do not infer absent metrics.** If a metric is not visible, leave it blank and note that in `Observacoes`. Later panel versions drop metrics outright (the September-2026 profile panel no longer exposes `Alcance` / `Contas alcancadas` — only `Visualizadores`, plus `Contas Meta alcancadas` on some posts): record the absence, never file a neighbouring metric under the old name.
- **The account panel and the per-post base are different measurements, not two attempts at one number.** Panel = views *occurring* in the window, over all content (Stories, Videos, Facebook cross-posts, and posts published months earlier); base = views *accumulated* by posts published inside the period, frozen at capture time. Interactions reconcile well (17.779 panel vs 18.414 base, ~3,5%), views never do (1.315.639 vs 497.290) - if you are asked why, explain the four axes (janela, escopo, unidade, unicidade) instead of hunting for a parsing bug.
- **The panel's numbers are abbreviated and partly hidden.** The ranked content list shows `99 mil`, `5,1 mil`, `--`; percentages stand in for the content-type split. Treat them as indicative, never as exact columns, and open the content's own insights when an exact value matters. `--` in the list is the same class of absence as a `--` panel, not a zero.
- **`Visualizadores` and `Contas com engajamento` are unique-per-content counts:** summing them across posts double-counts the same person and can exceed the account-level unique figure. Report them as a sum *of per-post uniques*, labelled as such, or not at all.
- **The panel's content page paints empty on the first read.** Right after navigation `document.body.innerText` is 1 character; poll (busy-wait ~3 s, or re-read) until the ranked list appears, the same way the per-post panel is polled.
- **The archived-stories grid cannot be counted by scrolling it.** `/archive/stories/` is virtualised: a full DOM sweep that reached the bottom and accumulated ids returned 122 of the month's real 270 stories and looked complete. Take the quantity from the app's own `day_shells` payload (`payload.items[].media_count`, one entry per day, the whole archive) and the per-story media from `reels_media` per day, then assert the two agree; a DOM sweep is navigation, not coverage. Recipe and collector: `references/archived-stories-capture.md`, `scripts/coletar_stories_arquivados.js`.
- **Long injected console scripts arrive truncated.** A big one-shot JS block fails as `SyntaxError: "undefined" is not valid JSON` or a generic controller error, which reads like a page problem but is the script being cut before it runs. Define one short helper per call (`window.__ex = function (txt) {...}`), call it in a short follow-up, and probe the real field names with `Object.keys(obj)` before looping over a captured payload — assuming a field name cost three rounds.
- **Authentication blockers are real blockers.** Stop for user login rather than faking progress.

## Verification Checklist

- Target profile confirmed.
- Exactly the requested number of recent posts collected.
- Workbook created in the requested folder.
- Workbook re-opened successfully.
- Final reply includes the exact output path.

### Completeness audit ("were all posts really captured?")

When the user asks you to *check* a finished period, re-run the check against the artifacts on disk —
never restate the earlier verdict, and never answer from the counts you already sent.

- Prove coverage by **set equality, not by totals**:
  `set(grid items for the period) == set(base media_id) == set(normalized captures media_id)`, printed as
  a boolean, plus the two difference sets (`in the grid, not captured` and `captured, not in the grid`),
  which must both be empty. Equal totals hide a swap; equal sets do not.
- Explain every absence with **fill counts segmented by dimension**: per metric, count filled rows and
  split by own/collab and by media type. An absence landing exactly on one segment (profile-activity
  missing in every collaboration and in no owned post) is a panel rule, not a capture failure — say which
  one it is instead of leaving a blank the user will read as data loss.
- Reconcile against the **previous version of the base**: every row of the earlier window must still be
  present, and name the fields that improved — the earlier run's empty likes column now filled is the
  proof the new pass earned its keep. A *value* changing on the overlap means the parser changed, not that
  the post moved.
- Report the period as `N/N` only when the set equality holds. A post whose panel returns placeholders
  after a re-read is `N/N-1`, named, with its documented status — never rounded up to "complete".

## References

- See `references/field-mapping.md` for a compact mapping of common Instagram insight labels to spreadsheet columns and collection notes.
- See `references/insights-panel-parsing.md` for the full post-level panel layout, the parsing rules (header-vs-likes, the `Facebook` overwrite, placeholder rejection), a reusable snippet, and the provenance rules.
- See `references/insights-collection-playbook.md` for the verified per-post flow (empty SEO shell, "Ver insights" clicked via JS), the three coexisting JSON shapes, the grid-scroll audit, the **shortcode → `media_id` → date** recipe, and how to resume a month collected across several sittings.
- See `references/workstation-browser-capture.md` for the embedded-browser capture flow, the two-call click-then-read pattern that avoids the navigation race, and the local JSONL sink that keeps captures out of the conversation.
- See `references/pitfalls-datas-autoria-grid.md` for publication-date truth (`<time datetime>` beats `og:description`), the authorship test, grid append behaviour, and the `execute_code`/`openpyxl` boundary.
- See `references/infinite-scroll-collection.md` and `references/post-level-insights-capture.md` for the persistent-scroll collector and the per-post capture/parse details.
- See `references/incremental-run-and-pipeline-copies.md` for extending a period that is already partly collected: window/boundary proofs, copying (never overwriting) the pipeline for a follow-up run, sweep-vs-previous-run overlap verification, and a coverage audit that spans both runs.

{"content": "1|# Stories arquivados (grade "Itens arquivados") — quantidade, midia e insights
2|
3|Camada propria: stories nao tem curtidas/comentarios publicos nem aparecem na base post-a-post.
4|Medir stories exige tres fontes diferentes, nesta ordem.
5|
6|## Regra central: a grade NAO serve como contagem
7|
8|A grade `/archive/stories/` renderiza por janela (lista virtualizada). Uma varredura DOM completa —
9|inclusive rolando ate o fim e acumulando ids em varias passadas — devolveu 122 de **270** stories de
10|um mesmo mes e parecia completa. Nunca derive quantidade de stories da grade; use-a apenas para
11|navegar visualmente.
12|
13|## Fonte autoritativa: `day_shells` (capturada, nunca reproduzida)
14|
15|- O proprio app chama, ao paginar a grade:
16|  `GET /api/v1/archive/reel/day_shells/?timezone_offset=-10800&__d=www&...`
17|- Resposta: `payload.items[]` = `{timestamp, media_count, id: "archiveDay:<id>", reel_type, latest_reel_media}`,
18|  dias mais recentes primeiro, `more_available:false` no fim, cobrindo o arquivo INTEIRO da conta
19|  (uma conta institucional real: 1567 dias, 2018 -> 2026).
20|- **`media_count` por dia e a contagem oficial.** Some o mes para o total
21|  (ex.: setembro = 19 dias com stories, 270 stories; um so dia pode concentrar 76).
22|- Repetir essa URL do console devolve payload **vazio**: `__s`/`__hsi`/`__req` sao parametros de uso
23|  unico/anti-abuso. Nao perca tempo com replay — instale um hook de `fetch`/XHR que guarde o **corpo
24|  completo** das respostas de `day_shells` e force a grade a paginar (rolar ate o fim) para o app
25|disparar a chamada; depois exporte o corpo guardado (blob + download).
26|- Aceite: soma de `media_count` do mes == numero de stories extraidos de `reels_media`.
27|
28|## Midia e metrica por story: `reels_media` (essa aceita replay)
29|
30|- `POST /api/v1/feed/reels_media/`, body `reel_ids=["archiveDay:<id>"]`, `credentials:'include'`,
31|  headers `x-csrftoken` (do cookie `csrftoken`) + `x-ig-app-id: 936619743392459`.
32|- Devolve `reels["archiveDay:<id>"].items[]` com:
33|  `pk` (media id), `id` (`<media_id>_<user_id>`), `taken_at`, `media_type` (1 imagem, 2 video),
34|  `viewer_count` (visualizacoes do story), `image_versions2.candidates[0].url` /
35|  `video_versions[0].url` — **URLs completas**, ao contrario das capas da grade, que chegam truncadas
36|  e retornam 403 no download.
37|- Uma chamada por dia, sequencial. O JSON bruto e pesado (~36 KB por story; 270 stories ~ 11 MB):
38|  **nunca transfira o bruto** — extraia em pagina so os campos compactos e so entao faca blob+download
39|  (11 MB -> 423 KB).
40|- `candidates[0]` ja e a maior resolucao: serve para baixar a capa e descrever o story por visao.
41|
42|## Insights por story (o painel de "Ver insights")
43|
44|- `POST /api/graphql`, query **`PolarisMediaInsightsBaseSurfaceQuery`**,
45|  `variables={"query_params":{"id":"<media_id>"},"is_creator_viewing_insights":true}`,
46|  com `x-csrftoken` / `x-fb-lsd` (do HTML) / `x-ig-app-id`.
47|- **Um `media_id` por chamada.** Lote com varios ids falha com `variable_value_out_of_range`; a query
48|  "Root" da mesma familia devolve so metadados — e a `BaseSurface` que traz as metricas.
49|- Traz o mesmo que a tela: visualizacoes, visualizadores, alcance, split seguidores/nao seguidores,
50|  interacoes, curtidas no story, respostas, compartilhamentos, cliques em link, visitas ao perfil,
51|  novos seguidores, **navegacao** (avanco / voltar / proximo / saiu) e **toques em figurinhas**
52|  (com quem tocou).
53|- Colete em background (`window.__COLL` sequencial, 1 id por chamada) e va lendo o progresso;
54|  ~0,5 s por story.
55|
56|## Transferencia, decoding e juncao
57|
58|- A CSP da pagina bloqueia `fetch` cross-origin: sink HTTP local nao serve. Use blob + `a.click()`
59|  (arquivo `.tmp` em Downloads) e copie para o scratch.
60|- Data do story: `(int(media_id) >> 23) + 1314220021721` = **milissegundos** — divida por 1000 antes de
61|  formatar (sem dividir: `Invalid argument: timestamp out of range`). Formate em BRT (UTC-3).
62|- Use o `media_id` como chave de juncao entre grade, `reels_media` e insights.
63|- `taken_at` e o dia do `archiveDay` concordam; quando divergirem, o `media_id` manda.
64|
65|## Pitfalls
66|
67|- **Script injetado longo e truncado antes de chegar a pagina.** Um bloco JS grande de uma vez chega
68|  cortado e falha com `SyntaxError: "undefined" is not valid JSON` ou erro generico do controller.
69|  Defina um helper curto por chamada (`window.__ex = function (txt) { ... }`), chame-o numa chamada
70|  seguinte, e confirme o nome real dos campos com um probe de uma linha (`Object.keys(R[k])`) antes de
71|  iterar — o campo guardado era `txt`, e tres tentativas se perderam assumindo `t`.
72|- **Varredura DOM no fim da lista nao e prova de cobertura.** Fechar o mes so com a soma de
73|  `media_count` do `day_shells` (e ela contra a extracao por dia).
74|- **Nao misture as camadas.** O total de stories do mes nao entra na base post-a-post nem no painel da
75|  conta; e uma terceira medida, guardada em sua propria captura.", "total_lines": 75, "file_size": 4975, "truncated": false, "is_binary": false, "is_image": false}

REGRA CENTRAL: a verificacao NUNCA reusa a fonte da coleta. Ela cruza tres fontes
independentes e falha se qualquer uma discordar:

  EXPECTATIVA  day_shells      -> media_count oficial por dia (a plataforma que manda)
  INVENTARIO   reels_media     -> uma chamada por dia; deve devolver exatamente media_count
  CONTEUDO     insights        -> um registro por midia, conjunto identico ao inventario

Uso:
  python verificar_completude.py --periodo 2026-09 --dir <pasta-da-coleta>
  python verificar_completude.py --periodo 2026-09 --dir . --json

Arquivos padrao dentro de --dir:
  day_shells_<periodo>.json   {"buckets":[{"dia_utc","id","media_count"}]}
  midias_<periodo>.json       {"por_dia":{"YYYY-MM-DD":[{pk,taken_at,img,vid,tipo}]}}
  insights_<periodo>.json     {"<media_id>": {...metricas...}}

Saida: VERIFICACAO-<periodo>.md, VERIFICACAO-<periodo>.json
Exit code: 0 = COMPLETO | 2 = INCOMPLETO | 1 = erro de uso/leitura
"""

import argparse
import datetime as dt
import hashlib
import json
import os
import sys

EPOCH_MS = 1314220021721  # epoch usado nos media_id do Instagram (ms)
FUSO_BRT = -3             # America/Sao_Paulo


# ----------------------------------------------------------------- utilidades

def ler_json(caminho):
    with open(caminho, "r", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        return json.load(fh)


def sha256(caminho):
    h = hashlib.sha256()
    with open(caminho, "rb") as fh:
        for bloco in iter(lambda: fh.read(1 << 20), b""):
            h.update(bloco)
    return h.hexdigest()


def dia_utc(ts):
    return dt.datetime.fromtimestamp(int(ts), dt.timezone.utc).strftime("%Y-%m-%d")


def dia_brt(ts):
    return (dt.datetime.fromtimestamp(int(ts), dt.timezone.utc)
            + dt.timedelta(hours=FUSO_BRT)).strftime("%Y-%m-%d")


def dia_do_media_id(media_id):
    """media_id -> data (UTC) segundo a codificacao de 41 bits + epoch do Instagram."""
    try:
        ms = (int(str(media_id).split("_")[0]) >> 23) + EPOCH_MS
        return dt.datetime.fromtimestamp(ms / 1000.0, dt.timezone.utc).strftime("%Y-%m-%d")
    except Exception:
        return None


def mes_anterior(periodo):
    a, m = int(periodo[:4]), int(periodo[5:7])
    return f"{a - 1}-12" if m == 1 else f"{a}-{m - 1:02d}"


def mes_seguinte(periodo):
    a, m = int(periodo[:4]), int(periodo[5:7])
    return f"{a + 1}-01" if m == 12 else f"{a}-{m + 1:02d}"


# -------------------------------------------------------------------- coleta

def carregar_buckets(caminho):
    dados = ler_json(caminho)
    bruto = dados.get("buckets") or dados.get("items") or []
    buckets = []
    for b in bruto:
        dia = b.get("dia_utc") or b.get("day") or b.get("dia")
        if dia is None and b.get("timestamp"):
            dia = dia_utc(b["timestamp"])
        if dia is None:
            continue
        buckets.append({
            "dia": dia[:10],
            "id": b.get("id"),
            "media_count": int(b.get("media_count", 0)),
        })
    return buckets


def carregar_midias(caminho):
    dados = ler_json(caminho)
    por_dia = dados.get("por_dia") or dados.get("por_dia_setembro") or {}
    fora = dados.get("stories_fora_de_setembro") or []
    midias = []
    for dia, lista in por_dia.items():
        for m in lista:
            midias.append({
                "pk": str(m.get("pk") or m.get("id") or "").split("_")[0],
                "taken_at": int(m["taken_at"]) if m.get("taken_at") else None,
                "tipo": m.get("tipo") or m.get("media_type"),
                "img": m.get("img") or m.get("img_url"),
                "vid": m.get("vid"),
                "dia_rotulo": dia,
            })
    for m in fora:
        midias.append({
            "pk": str(m.get("pk") or m.get("id") or "").split("_")[0],
            "taken_at": int(m["taken_at"]) if m.get("taken_at") else None,
            "tipo": m.get("tipo") or m.get("media_type"),
            "img": m.get("img"),
            "vid": m.get("vid"),
            "dia_rotulo": m.get("data_brt"),
        })
    return midias


def carregar_insights(caminho):
    dados = ler_json(caminho)
    if isinstance(dados, dict) and "insights" in dados and isinstance(dados["insights"], dict):
        dados = dados["insights"]
    limpos = {}
    for k, v in dados.items():
        if not isinstance(v, dict):
            continue
        mid = str(v.get("media_id") or k).split("_")[0]
        limpos[mid] = v
    return limpos


def tem_conteudo(registro):
    """Um registro de insights valido precisa trazer pelo menos uma metrica real."""
    if not isinstance(registro, dict):
        return False
    if registro.get("erro") or registro.get("erros") or registro.get("error"):
        return False
    corpo = registro.get("u") or registro.get("metricas") or registro
    if not isinstance(corpo, dict):
        return False
    return any(corpo.get(k) for k in corpo.keys() if k not in ("media_id", "reel_id", "tags"))


# --------------------------------------------------------------------- checks

def verificar(periodo, dir_coleta, nomes):
    caminho_ds = os.path.join(dir_coleta, nomes["day_shells"])
    caminho_mid = os.path.join(dir_coleta, nomes["midias"])
    caminho_ins = os.path.join(dir_coleta, nomes["insights"])

    for c in (caminho_ds, caminho_mid, caminho_ins):
        if not os.path.exists(c):
            print(f"ERRO: arquivo obrigatorio ausente: {c}", file=sys.stderr)
            return None, 1

    buckets = carregar_buckets(caminho_ds)
    midias = carregar_midias(caminho_mid)
    insights = carregar_insights(caminho_ins)

    # classificacao por DIA UTC do taken_at (mesma convencao do day_shells)
    por_dia_utc = {}
    for m in midias:
        if m["taken_at"] is None:
            continue
        por_dia_utc.setdefault(dia_utc(m["taken_at"]), []).append(m)

    buckets_periodo = [b for b in buckets if b["dia"][:7] == periodo]
    buckets_borda = {
        "anterior": sorted([b for b in buckets if b["dia"][:7] == mes_anterior(periodo)],
                           key=lambda b: b["dia"], reverse=True)[:1],
        "seguinte": sorted([b for b in buckets if b["dia"][:7] == mes_seguinte(periodo)],
                           key=lambda b: b["dia"])[:1],
    }

    checks = []

    def add(nome, ok, detalhe, fatal=True):
        checks.append({"check": nome, "ok": bool(ok), "detalhe": detalhe, "fatal": fatal})

    # 1. dia a dia: media_count oficial == midias extraidas naquele dia UTC
    linhas, divergencias, esperado_total = [], [], 0
    for b in sorted(buckets_periodo, key=lambda x: x["dia"]):
        obtido = len(por_dia_utc.get(b["dia"], []))
        esperado_total += b["media_count"]
        linhas.append({"dia": b["dia"], "esperado": b["media_count"], "midias": obtido,
                       "ok": obtido == b["media_count"]})
        if obtido != b["media_count"]:
            divergencias.append(f"{b['dia']}: esperado {b['media_count']}, obtido {obtido}")
    add("ESPERATIVA_POR_DIA", not divergencias,
        "todo dia do mes com media_count == midias extraidas" if not divergencias
        else "; ".join(divergencias))

    # 2. sem buraco no total
    ids_unicos = {m["pk"] for m in midias if m["pk"]}
    add("SEM_BURACO", len(ids_unicos) == esperado_total,
        f"esperado {esperado_total}, inventario tem {len(ids_unicos)}")

    # 3. sem duplicata
    add("SEM_DUPLICATA", len(ids_unicos) == len([m for m in midias if m["pk"]]),
        f"{len(midias)} entradas, {len(ids_unicos)} ids unicos")

    # 4. toda midia utilizavel
    incompletas = [m["pk"] for m in midias
                   if not m["pk"] or not m["taken_at"] or (not m["img"] and not m["vid"])]
    add("MIDIA_UTILIZAVEL", not incompletas,
        f"{len(incompletas)} sem pk/taken_at/url" + (f": {incompletas[:5]}" if incompletas else ""))

    # 5. conjunto de insights == conjunto de midias
    faltam = sorted(ids_unicos - set(insights))
    extras = sorted(set(insights) - ids_unicos)
    add("INSIGHTS_EXATOS", not faltam and not extras,
        f"faltam {len(faltam)}, sobram {len(extras)}"
        + (f" | primeiros faltantes: {faltam[:5]}" if faltam else "")
        + (f" | primeiros extras: {extras[:5]}" if extras else ""))

    # 6. insights com conteudo real (nao vazio / nao erro)
    vazios = sorted([k for k in insights if not tem_conteudo(insights[k])])
    add("INSIGHTS_COM_CONTEUDO", not vazios,
        f"{len(vazios)} registros sem metrica" + (f": {vazios[:5]}" if vazios else ""))

    # 7. codificacao do media_id coerente com o taken_at
    incoerentes = [m["pk"] for m in midias
                   if m["taken_at"] and dia_do_media_id(m["pk"]) != dia_utc(m["taken_at"])]
    add("MEDIA_ID_COERENTE", not incoerentes,
        f"{len(incoerentes)} divergencias" + (f": {incoerentes[:5]}" if incoerentes else ""))

    # 8. borda do mes (nao fatal: avisa para o operador conferir)
    fora_brt = {}
    for m in midias:
        if m["taken_at"] is None:
            continue
        d = dia_brt(m["taken_at"])
        if d[:7] != periodo and d:
            fora_brt[d] = fora_brt.get(d, 0) + 1
    add("BORDA_DE_MES", True,
        f"buckets vizinhos: anterior={[b['dia'] for b in buckets_borda['anterior']]} "
        f"seguinte={[b['dia'] for b in buckets_borda['seguinte']]} | "
        f"midias com data BRT fora do periodo: {fora_brt or 'nenhuma'}", fatal=False)

    por_dia_brt = {}
    for m in midias:
        if m["taken_at"] is None:
            continue
        d = dia_brt(m["taken_at"])
        if d[:7] == periodo:
            por_dia_brt[d] = por_dia_brt.get(d, 0) + 1

    fatal_falhou = [c for c in checks if c["fatal"] and not c["ok"]]
    veredito = "COMPLETO" if not fatal_falhou else "INCOMPLETO"

    manifesto = {
        "gerado_em": dt.datetime.now(dt.timezone.utc).isoformat(timespec="seconds"),
        "periodo": periodo,
        "dir": os.path.abspath(dir_coleta),
        "veredito": veredito,
        "fontes": {n: {"arquivo": os.path.basename(c), "sha256": sha256(c),
                       "bytes": os.path.getsize(c)}
                   for n, c in (("day_shells", caminho_ds), ("midias", caminho_mid),
                                ("insights", caminho_ins))},
        "totais": {
            "dias_no_periodo": len(buckets_periodo),
            "esperado_day_shells": esperado_total,
            "midias_inventario": len(ids_unicos),
            "insights_capturados": len(insights),
            "insights_faltantes": len(faltam),
            "midias_data_brt_no_periodo": sum(por_dia_brt.values()),
        },
        "por_dia": [{"dia": l["dia"], "esperado": l["esperado"], "midias": l["midias"],
                     "insights": sum(1 for m in por_dia_utc.get(l["dia"], []) if m["pk"] in insights),
                     "ok": l["ok"]} for l in linhas],
        "por_dia_brt": dict(sorted(por_dia_brt.items())),
        "checks": checks,
        "faltantes": faltam,
    }
    return manifesto, (0 if veredito == "COMPLETO" else 2)


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ relatorio

def relatorio_md(man):
    L = []
    selo = "✅ COMPLETO" if man["veredito"] == "COMPLETO" else "❌ INCOMPLETO"
    L.append(f"# Verificação de completude — {man['periodo']}")
    L.append("")
    L.append(f"**{selo}** — gerado em {man['gerado_em']} (UTC)")
    L.append("")
    t = man["totais"]
    L.append(f"- Dias com stories no mês: **{t['dias_no_periodo']}**")
    L.append(f"- Esperado (day_shells `media_count`): **{t['esperado_day_shells']}**")
    L.append(f"- Inventário (reels_media): **{t['midias_inventario']}**")
    L.append(f"- Insights capturados: **{t['insights_capturados']}** "
             f"(faltam {t['insights_faltantes']})")
    L.append("")
    L.append("| dia (UTC) | esperado | mídias | insights | |")
    L.append("|---|---|---|---|---|")
    for l in man["por_dia"]:
        L.append(f"| {l['dia']} | {l['esperado']} | {l['midias']} | {l['insights']} | "
                 f"{'ok' if l['ok'] else '**divergente**'} |")
    L.append("")
    L.append("## Checks")
    L.append("")
    for c in man["checks"]:
        marca = "ok" if c["ok"] else ("**FALHOU**" if c["fatal"] else "aviso")
        L.append(f"- `{c['check']}` — {marca}: {c['detalhe']}")
    L.append("")
    L.append("## Procedência (sha256)")
    L.append("")
    for n, f in man["fontes"].items():
        L.append(f"- `{f['arquivo']}` ({f['bytes']} bytes) — `{f['sha256'][:16]}…`")
    L.append("")
    L.append("Gerado por `verificar_completude.py` (skill instagram-post-metrics-reporting).")
    L.append("Nenhum dado desta captura pode ir para a camada canônica sem este veredito.")
    return "\n".join(L) + "\n"


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Prova de completude de captura do Instagram")
    ap.add_argument("--periodo", required=True, help="YYYY-MM (ex.: 2026-09)")
    ap.add_argument("--dir", default=".", help="pasta da coleta")
    ap.add_argument("--day-shells", default=None)
    ap.add_argument("--midias", default=None)
    ap.add_argument("--insights", default=None)
    ap.add_argument("--json", action="store_true", help="imprime o manifesto no stdout")
    args = ap.parse_args()

    p = args.periodo
    nomes = {
        "day_shells": args.day_shells or f"day_shells_{p}.json",
        "midias": args.midias or f"midias_{p}.json",
        "insights": args.insights or f"insights_{p}.json",
    }
    man, code = verificar(p, args.dir, nomes)
    if man is None:
        return code

    saida_json = os.path.join(args.dir, f"VERIFICACAO-{p}.json")
    saida_md = os.path.join(args.dir, f"VERIFICACAO-{p}.md")
    with open(saida_json, "w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        json.dump(man, fh, ensure_ascii=False, indent=1)
    with open(saida_md, "w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        fh.write(relatorio_md(man))

    if args.json:
        print(json.dumps(man, ensure_ascii=False, indent=1))
    else:
        t = man["totais"]
        print(f"{man['veredito']} {p}: esperado {t['esperado_day_shells']} | "
              f"midias {t['midias_inventario']} | insights {t['insights_capturados']} "
              f"| faltam {t['insights_faltantes']}")
        for c in man["checks"]:
            if not c["ok"]:
                print(f"  {'FALHOU' if c['fatal'] else 'aviso'} {c['check']}: {c['detalhe']}")
        print(f"  -> {saida_md}")
    return code


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

{"content": "# Prova de completude — como parar de desconfiar das capturas

Regra que este documento existe para sustentar:

> **Nenhum dado desta skill entra na camada canônica sem um veredito `COMPLETO` emitido por
> `scripts/verificar_completude.py`.**

A dúvida "será que pegou tudo?" não se resolve olhando o resultado — ele *parece* completo
mesmo quando não está. Resolve-se com um artefato que cruza fontes independentes e **falha
alto** quando discordam.

## O que deu errado em 02/10/2026 (para não repetir)

Uma varredura de DOM em `/archive/stories/` devolveu 184 ids e *parecia* o mês inteiro. O
mês tinha 272 stories. Pior: a coleta de insights foi feita a partir dessa grade, então
cobriu só os dias que ela expunha (≥ 11/09) — **121 de 272 (44%), com 0% de cobertura em
sete dias** — e ninguém percebeu, porque os 121 registros estavam certos e consistentes.

Três armadilhas que produziram isso:

1. **Lista virtualizada.** A grade só materializa no DOM a janela visível. Rolar até o fim
   não garante nada: o recorte depende do tamanho da janela e do momento.
2. **Offset aplicado duas vezes.** O `timestamp` do `day_shells` é um carimbo de início de
   dia (`…T00:01:40Z`). Subtrair o offset de BRT e ler campos UTC joga **todo bucket um dia
   para trás**: descartou o bucket de 01/09 (3 stories) e puxou o de 01/10 (1 story) para
   dentro. As duas fontes "concordavam" porque o mesmo fuso errado foi aplicado nas duas.
3. **Fonte única.** Expectativa e inventário vinham do mesmo lugar, então concordar não
   provava nada.

## O mecanismo: três fontes, cruzadas

| Papel | Endpoint | O que prova |
|---|---|---|
| EXPECTATIVA | `GET /api/v1/archive/reel/day_shells/` | `media_count` oficial por dia — **a plataforma manda** |
| INVENTÁRIO | `POST /api/v1/feed/reels_media/` (1 por bucket) | devolve exatamente `media_count` mídias daquele dia |
| CONTEÚDO | `POST /api/graphql` `PolarisMediaInsightsBaseSurfaceQuery` | 1 registro por mídia, com métricas reais |

O verificador nunca reusa a fonte da coleta para se auto-validar. Ele compara as três.

### Checks (todos fatais, exceto o último)

| Check | O que exige |
|---|---|
| `ESPERATIVA_POR_DIA` | para cada dia do mês, `media_count` == nº de mídias daquele dia |
| `SEM_BURACO` | total de ids únicos == soma de `media_count` |
| `SEM_DUPLICATA` | nº de entradas == nº de ids únicos |
| `MIDIA_UTILIZAVEL` | toda mídia tem `pk`, `taken_at` e URL de imagem ou vídeo |
| `INSIGHTS_EXATOS` | conjunto de ids com insights == conjunto de ids do inventário |
| `INSIGHTS_COM_CONTEUDO` | nenhum registro vazio ou com erro |
| `MEDIA_ID_COERENTE` | `media_id` decodificado bate com o `taken_at` em 100% |
| `BORDA_DE_MES` | *(aviso)* reporta os buckets vizinhos e o que ficou fora do período |

**O `--offset` tem que ser o mesmo `timezone_offset` da coleta.** O dia do bucket é o dia
**local** da conta, não o dia UTC. Com UTC, 8 stories de 12/09 apareciam como 13/09 e 5 de
29/09 como 30/09 — divergência falsa que faria o verificador reprovar uma coleta correta.
Verificador com offset errado é pior que nenhum: ele "prova" um erro inexistente e treina
você a ignorá-lo.

```
1. console do app (instagram.com logado):  cole scripts/coletar_stories_periodo.js
2. await __IG.periodo('2026-09')
3. __IG.baixar('day_shells_2026-09.json', __IG.saida.day_shells)

5. python scripts/verificar_completude.py --periodo 2026-09 --dir <pasta>
   -> exit 0  = COMPLETO  -> pode publicar na camada canônica
   -> exit 2  = INCOMPLETO -> NÃO publicar; o relatório diz exatamente o que falta
```

Saída: `VERIFICACAO-<periodo>.md` (tabela dia a dia + checks + sha256 das fontes) e
`VERIFICACAO-<periodo>.json` (manifesto legível por máquina).

O manifesto é o selo: ele amarra o veredito aos **hashes** dos três arquivos. Se qualquer

```
capturas/instagram/<conta>/<periodo>/

  midias_<periodo>.json        inventário (mídias por dia, com URLs)
```

{"content": "#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""sink_save.py - TRANSFERENCIA PADRAO de payload do navegador para o disco.

POR QUE ESTE E O PADRAO
-----------------------
No app Electron, `a.download = ...; a.click()` abre um dialogo NATIVO de "Salvar"
que o agente nao consegue clicar: o arquivo nunca chega ao disco e o erro e silencioso
(nenhum .tmp aparece na pasta Downloads, nenhum erro no console). Por isso **nao use
download de blob nem Base64 colado no chat** para payload grande.

O canal que funciona: o navegador NAVEGA para este sink local.
O CSP do Instagram restringe `connect-src` (fetch/XHR/beacon) e `frame-src` (iframe),
mas NAO restringe navegacao de topo -- entao `location.href = 'http://127.0.0.1:PORT/salvar?...'`
entrega o arquivo. window.open costuma ser bloqueado (popup) e cai no mesmo comportamento:
navega a aba atual.

USO (padrao da skill, sempre nesta ordem)
-----------------------------------------
1. Suba o sink ANTES de coletar, apontando para a pasta da rodada:

       python sink_save.py 8766 "<pasta-da-rodada>"

2. No console da pagina, ao terminar a coleta, empacote e entregue:

       await window.__SINK.entregar('insights_2026-09.json', payload)

   (o helper __SINK fica disponivel depois de `await __IG.carregar()` do coletor
    coletar_stories_periodo.js; ele ja aplica gzip + base64 + encodeURIComponent)

3. Confirme no disco. O sink valida JSON e devolve `bytes` + `sha256`; compare o
   `sha256`/`bytes` com o que o console reportou ANTES de navegar.

4. Depois da navegacao a aba fica no sink: volte com `browser_navigate` para
   https://www.instagram.com/... (o estado JS da pagina se perde, por isso o passo 3).

REGRAS
------
- `nome` e sempre reduzido a basename: o sink nunca escreve fora da pasta de destino.
- Aceita base64 puro ou base64 de gzip (detectado pelo magic 1f 8b).
- Se o arquivo terminar em .json, o JSON e validado antes de gravar (falha = nada gravado).
- Porta padrao 8766. Se ja houver um sink rodando nela, reaproveite-o.
"""
import base64
import gzip
import hashlib
import json
import os
import sys
import urllib.parse
from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, ThreadingHTTPServer

DESTINO = os.path.abspath(sys.argv[2] if len(sys.argv) > 2 else ".")
PORTA_PADRAO = 8766


class Handler(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
    protocol_version = "HTTP/1.1"
    max_line = 8 * 1024 * 1024  # o payload grande viaja na query string

    def log_message(self, fmt, *a):
        pass

    def _responder(self, code, obj):
        corpo = json.dumps(obj, ensure_ascii=False).encode("utf-8")
        self.send_response(code)
        self.send_header("Content-Type", "application/json; charset=utf-8")
        self.send_header("Access-Control-Allow-Origin", "*")
        self.send_header("Content-Length", str(len(corpo)))
        self.end_headers()
        self.wfile.write(corpo)

    def do_GET(self):
        u = urllib.parse.urlparse(self.path)
        q = urllib.parse.parse_qs(u.query, max_num_fields=10)

        if u.path == "/health":
            return self._responder(200, {"ok": True, "ping": "ping-ok", "destino": DESTINO})

        if u.path != "/salvar":
            return self._responder(404, {"erro": "rota desconhecida", "rotas": ["/health", "/salvar"]})

        nome = os.path.basename((q.get("nome") or [""])[0])
        dado = (q.get("d") or [""])[0]
        if not nome or not dado:
            return self._responder(400, {"erro": "informe nome= e d="})

        try:
            bruto = base64.b64decode(dado, validate=False)
        except Exception as e:
            return self._responder(400, {"erro": f"base64 invalido: {e}"})

        gzipado = bruto[:2] == b"\x1f\x8b"
        if gzipado:
            try:
                bruto = gzip.decompress(bruto)
            except Exception as e:
                return self._responder(400, {"erro": f"gzip corrompido: {e}"})

        if nome.endswith(".json"):
            try:
                json.loads(bruto.decode("utf-8"))
            except Exception as e:
                return self._responder(400, {"erro": f"json invalido: {e}"})

        os.makedirs(DESTINO, exist_ok=True)
        caminho = os.path.join(DESTINO, nome)
        with open(caminho, "wb") as fh:
            fh.write(bruto)

        return self._responder(200, {"ok": True, "arquivo": caminho, "bytes": len(bruto),
                                     "gzip_entrada": gzipado,
                                     "sha256": hashlib.sha256(bruto).hexdigest()})


if __name__ == "__main__":
    porta = int(sys.argv[1]) if len(sys.argv) > 1 else PORTA_PADRAO
    print(f"sink_save: http://127.0.0.1:{porta} -> {DESTINO}", flush=True)
    ThreadingHTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", porta), Handler).serve_forever()

2|name: instagram-post-metrics-reporting
3|description: Use when exporting Instagram post metrics to a spreadsheet.
4|version: 1.0.0

14|
15|# Instagram Post Metrics Reporting
16|
17|Collect metrics from recent Instagram posts and deliver a verified spreadsheet.
18|Use this when the user wants the latest N posts from a profile summarized in Excel,
19|especially for professional/business accounts where post-level insights are visible on web.
20|
21|## When to Use
22|
23|- The user asks for a spreadsheet of the latest Instagram posts.
24|- The task is to capture post metrics from a professional account and organize them.
25|- The output must land in `Downloads` or another user-facing folder and be verified.
26|- When the account is vault-managed (institutional accounts in a curated vault), the deliverable is the vault's **canonical base**, not a loose spreadsheet in `Downloads` — see the `acirv-notebook-vault` skill.
27|
28|## Prerequisites
29|
30|- The user is already authenticated in Instagram Web.
31|- The target account is accessible from the current session.
32|- If insights require a professional/business login or a permission wall appears, stop and ask the user to authenticate instead of guessing credentials.
33|- For `.xlsx` output, use Python + `openpyxl`.
34|
35|## Two Layers - Capture Both
36|
37|Instagram exposes two different layers, and they do **not** reconcile by summing:
38|
39|| | Camada 1 — post a post | Camada 2 — painel da conta |
40||---|---|---|
41|| Onde | `/<tipo>/<shortcode>/` ou `/insights/media/<media_id>/` | `/accounts/insights/?timeframe=30` |
42|| Unidade | o post, pelo `media_id` | a conta, no período |
43|| Escopo | feed + reels do grid | tudo: Posts, Reels, **Stories**, Vídeos, e o split Instagram/Facebook |
44|| Como conta | visualizações **acumuladas** do post até a coleta | visualizações **ocorridas** na janela, em todo o conteúdo (inclusive de meses anteriores) |
45|| Saída | base canônica por post | foto do painel (totais, %, listas de destaque) |
46|
47|The account panel is always larger - in a verified month it reported ~1,3M views over 30 days against
48|~500k summed from that period's posts (2,6x), because it adds Stories (~31% of its total), Facebook
49|cross-posts, the rolling-window effect, and views on content published before the period. **Never
50|present the two as the same number, and never "fix" one to match the other.**
51|
52|Capture **both** layers every time. The per-post base answers "how did each post perform"; the panel
53|answers "how did the account perform in the window" - and it is the number the user sees in the app,
54|so a report with only one of them always provokes the question of why they differ.
55|

61|## Core Workflow
62|
63|1. **Confirm access first**
64|   - Open Instagram Web and verify you can reach the target profile.
65|   - Confirm the account is the intended one before collecting data.
66|
67|2. **Find the complete owned-post set**
68|   - Prefer direct profile navigation.
69|   - Identify post URLs from links containing `/p/` or `/reel/` on the profile page.
70|   - When the request covers a whole year, date range, or says “all posts”, repeatedly force a downward scroll on the profile grid/feed so Instagram has time to lazy-load older posts. Continue persistent scrolling until several consecutive scrolls add no new owned-post URLs, or until posts clearly pass the requested start date.
71|   - After each scroll batch, harvest and deduplicate the newly loaded URLs; do not rely only on the first viewport.
72|   - Filter by the requested date range and verify chronological coverage before opening posts. Do not stop at “some recent posts”.
73|
74|3. **Open each post directly**
75|   - Navigate to the post URL itself.
76|   - Once loaded, inspect both the visible page text and DOM-extracted text.
77|
78|4. **Prefer text extraction over brittle clicking**
79|   - If `browser_snapshot` is sparse or misses rendered content, use `browser_console` to read `document.body.innerText` and relevant metadata.
80|   - On some Instagram post pages, the insight metrics are already present in the inline rendered text even when clicking **Ver insights** fails.
81|   - Before retrying clicks, inspect the current text; do not assume the metric is unavailable just because the snapshot is empty.
82|
83|5. **Normalize metrics carefully**
84|   - Capture the post identity: URL, shortcode, publication time text, timestamp when available, caption snippet.
85|   - Capture every visible metric with its label, not just headline totals.
86|   - Preserve raw extracted lines in addition to normalized columns so later review can reconcile ambiguities.
87|   - Prefer explicitly labeled insight values over public social proof text like “Curtido por X e outras Y pessoas”.
88|
89|6. **Build the workbook**
90|   - Create at least these sheets:
91|     - `Resumo`: one row per post with normalized fields.
92|     - `RawInsights`: raw label/value lines for auditability.
93|     - `Observacoes`: collection notes, caveats, timestamp, and source profile.
94|   - Keep the sheet human-readable: bold header row, freeze panes, autofilter, wrapped text for captions/notes.
95|
96|7. **Verify the artifact**
97|   - Re-open the workbook with `openpyxl.load_workbook`.
98|   - Confirm the file exists, sheet names are correct, and row counts are plausible.
99|   - Only then tell the user it is ready.
100|
101|8. **Capture the account-level panel (camada 2)**
102|   - Read `/accounts/insights/?timeframe=30` (also `7`, `14`, `90`) and record, with the read's date/time:
103|     `Visualizações` (with the Instagram/Facebook split), `Visualizadores`, `Interações`, `Contas com
104|     engajamento`, `Atividade do perfil` (visitas + toques em links), `Total de seguidores`, and the
105|     content-type split.
106|   - Read the ranked content lists:
107|     `/accounts/insights/content/?media_type=all&metric=views&sort_by=highest&timeframe=30&view_type=card`,
108|     then the same with `metric=interactions` and `media_type=posts|reels|stories|videos`.
109|   - Store the panel snapshot as its own file (`_painel_conta_<YYYY-MM-DD>_<timeframe>.json`) beside the
110|     captures - never inside the per-post base. Run `scripts/coletar_painel_conta.js` in the page for both
111|     blocks (overview + ranked list) instead of hand-writing the DOM walk; `references/account-level-insights-panel.md`
112|     holds the full recipe, the DOM layout and the reconciliation arithmetic.
113|
114|9. **Report both layers, with the reconciliation spelled out**
115|   - Give the per-post totals for the period and the panel totals for its window side by side, and state
116|     in one line why they differ (janela, Stories/Facebook, visualizacao por data, unicidade). A bare
117|     panel number next to a bare base number reads as a contradiction to the user.
118|
119|## Recommended Extraction Pattern
120|
121|When Instagram’s structured snapshot is too thin, extract with browser JS:
122|
123|- `document.body.innerText` for visible metrics and labels.
124|- `meta[property="og:description"]` / `og:title` for post summary text.
125|- `time` element for machine-readable post datetime when present.
126|- Link harvesting from the profile page to enumerate recent posts.
127|
128|## Pitfalls
129|
130|- **Sparse snapshots are not proof of missing data.** Instagram often renders useful text that the accessibility snapshot omits.
131|- **“Ver insights” may fail to click even when insights are already visible inline.** Inspect page text before retrying.
132|- **Metric labels vary slightly.** Preserve raw labels and map them conservatively instead of forcing guesses.
133|- **The profile grid can look complete while hiding everything.** The grid appends older items **only when the page is scrolled to its actual bottom** (`window.scrollTo(0, document.body.scrollHeight)` + ~1.5 s wait, repeated until `scrollHeight` stops growing). Small-step scrolling (250-700 px) leaves the page stuck at ~24 items and silently truncates the enumeration — that, not DOM virtualization, was the real cause of the apparent gaps. Scroll in batches of 3-4 bottom-jumps per call, harvest + dedupe after each, and stop once you pass the first post outside the requested period.
134|- **`og:description` dates are upload/scheduling dates, not publication dates.** A batch created on 23-28/ago published on 01-08/set looked like "missing August posts" and cost hours. Always date posts from the rendered `<time datetime>` (absolute dates for posts >7 days old also appear in the page text). See `references/pitfalls-datas-autoria-grid.md` for this plus the authorship test ("Ver insights" present = owned/co-authored; absent = third party merely tagging), date bracketing by grid position, and the fact that `openpyxl` is only reachable via `terminal`.
135|- **The panel's top line `Curtidas <n>` carries the COMMENT count, not likes.** On reels and many feed posts the header renders a single value under the label "Curtidas" whose number equals the post's comments (e.g. header `Curtidas 128` while the labeled block says `Curtidas 7.842` / `Comentários 128`). Never take `curtidas` from the header — always read it from the labeled breakdown block (`Interações com posts` / `Interações com reels` → `Curtidas`). Carousel/feed panels sometimes render two bare numbers (`77\n4`) which *are* likes/comments; treat only that form as a likes header.
136|- **The trailing `Facebook` sub-section silently overwrites real numbers.** Under `Perfil` the panel repeats `Visualizações`, `Reações` and `Comentários` with the *Facebook* cross-post numbers (tiny values). Parsing the whole text lets those clobber the Instagram values — one reel with 115.839 views and 128 comments was read as 252 views / 0 comments, and the month's view total came out 207.424 instead of 445.217. Truncate the text at the first `\nFacebook\n` before parsing.
137|- **`--`, `9+`, and `NN%` values are not metrics.** The panel emits `--` for hidden profile activity, `9+` as a "more metrics" placeholder (it also appears trailing, after a `Seguidores` label), and percentages for follower splits. Drop any of these from integer columns and record them as absent, otherwise `novos_seguidores` ends up as the string `96.2%`.
138|- **Persist every capture to disk as you go, never only in the chat.** Four posts were re-read successfully in conversation but their values were never written to a file, so the whole month had to be re-fetched. Write each batch to `_raw_bNN.jsonl` immediately; when re-reading, keep the longest capture per `media_id` (a complete re-read should win over a collapsed one).
139|- **Resume the previous run instead of restarting the month.** A month is collected across several sittings; the consolidated workbook often survives in the vault while the raw per-post files do not. Read the covered window from the consolidation before touching the browser, and when the prior working directory is not on disk, **ask the user where it is** — recreating the directory or re-implementing the pipeline silently re-collects already-parsed posts and duplicates the report. {"content": "140|- **A previous run's grid inventory is a snapshot, never an extendable base.** `_grid_inventario.json` records the grid as it stood at capture time (`cobertura_grid: [newest, oldest]`) and nothing newer can be derived from it, so collecting the *remaining* part of a period always needs a fresh top-down grid sweep down to the old boundary. Verify a claimed working directory by searching *inside* its path — a directory-**name** glob returns zero matches even when the folder exists, which reads as "missing" and wastes a round-trip with the user.
141|- **A follow-up run over the rest of a period is a copy of the pipeline, not an overwrite.** Copy the scripts to suffixed siblings and rewrite artifact names programmatically, asserting every expected token was found before writing (a silent no-op substitution re-reads the previous run's inputs and ships a report of the wrong window). Point the output at a **new** filename, adapt the validator's hardcoded counts and owned/collab split to the new window, and make the builder read the new window's worklist — filtering the full-period inventory selects posts this run never captured and fires its own completeness assertion. See `references/incremental-run-and-pipeline-copies.md`.
142|- **A fresh sweep earns trust by agreeing with the previous run on the overlap.** Shared positions must match media_id for media_id; a divergence means the shortcode → media_id/date derivation is wrong, not that the data moved. Collaborator posts carry a longer token — slice to the leading 11 characters before decoding.
143|- **Diff the grid inventory against the worklist before declaring a period closed.** A sweep can store a position with a *concatenated* token (the shortcode glued to the following id, e.g. `DdFXhdwp0L9-io7p…`), and any builder that filters the grid by that broken token drops the post silently — the period then looks complete one item short. Reconcile grid items → worklist → captured records by `media_id` (not by count), and capture the missing position explicitly instead of trusting the total.
144|- **The per-post panel renders standalone at `/insights/media/<media_id>/`.** No click on "Ver insights" is needed. Poll for the panel's own label (`Visualiza`) plus a length floor instead of sleeping and hoping; a page that is still mounting returns a short body that looks like missing data.
145|- **A `--` that survives a re-read is genuinely absent.** When a panel looks partial (`Interações --`, `Contas Meta alcançadas --`), wait a few seconds and read once more: a value that fills in was mid-render, a value that stays `--` is missing data (usual on collaborator posts) — record the absence and stop re-fetching that post.
146|- **When a whole panel is `--`, fall back to the public media endpoint instead of retrying forever.** A post owned by a third party where the account is only a co-author exposes no insights at all (`Visualizações --`, `Visualizadores --`, `Interações --`). Read the public media info (`/api/v1/media/<media_id>/info/` with the web `x-ig-app-id` header) for `play_count` / `like_count` / `comment_count`, plus `coauthors` to prove the account really is a co-author, and file those numbers as an explicitly labelled fallback — never as panel truth. Burn one control post that reads normally to prove the wall is post-specific and not rate limiting or a lost login.
147|- **Do not infer absent metrics.** If a metric is not visible, leave it blank and note that in `Observacoes`. Later panel versions drop metrics outright (the September-2026 profile panel no longer exposes `Alcance` / `Contas alcancadas` — only `Visualizadores`, plus `Contas Meta alcancadas` on some posts): record the absence, never file a neighbouring metric under the old name.
148|- **The account panel and the per-post base are different measurements, not two attempts at one number.** Panel = views *occurring* in the window, over all content (Stories, Videos, Facebook cross-posts, and posts published months earlier); base = views *accumulated* by posts published inside the period, frozen at capture time. Interactions reconcile well (17.779 panel vs 18.414 base, ~3,5%), views never do (1.315.639 vs 497.290) - if you are asked why, explain the four axes (janela, escopo, unidade, unicidade) instead of hunting for a parsing bug.
149|- **The panel's numbers are abbreviated and partly hidden.** The ranked content list shows `99 mil`, `5,1 mil`, `--`; percentages stand in for the content-type split. Treat them as indicative, never as exact columns, and open the content's own insights when an exact value matters. `--` in the list is the same class of absence as a `--` panel, not a zero.
150|- **`Visualizadores` and `Contas com engajamento` are unique-per-content counts:** summing them across posts double-counts the same person and can exceed the account-level unique figure. Report them as a sum *of per-post uniques*, labelled as such, or not at all.
151|- **The panel's content page paints empty on the first read.** Right after navigation `document.body.innerText` is 1 character; poll (busy-wait ~3 s, or re-read) until the ranked list appears, the same way the per-post panel is polled.
152|- **The archived-stories grid cannot be counted by scrolling it.** `/archive/stories/` is virtualised: a full DOM sweep that reached the bottom and accumulated ids returned 122 of the month's real 270 stories and looked complete. Take the quantity from the app's own `day_shells` payload (`payload.items[].media_count`, one entry per day, the whole archive) and the per-story media from `reels_media` per day, then assert the two agree; a DOM sweep is navigation, not coverage. Recipe and collector: `references/archived-stories-capture.md`, `scripts/coletar_stories_arquivados.js`.
153|- **Long injected console scripts arrive truncated.** A big one-shot JS block fails as `SyntaxError: "undefined" is not valid JSON` or a generic controller error, which reads like a page problem but is the script being cut before it runs. Define one short helper per call (`window.__ex = function (txt) {...}`), call it in a short follow-up, and probe the real field names with `Object.keys(obj)` before looping over a captured payload — assuming a field name cost three rounds.
154|- **Authentication blockers are real blockers.** Stop for user login rather than faking progress.
155|
156|## Verification Checklist
157|
158|- Target profile confirmed.
159|- Exactly the requested number of recent posts collected.
160|- Workbook created in the requested folder.
161|- Workbook re-opened successfully.
162|- Final reply includes the exact output path.
163|
164|### Completeness audit ("were all posts really captured?")
165|
166|When the user asks you to *check* a finished period, re-run the check against the artifacts on disk —
167|never restate the earlier verdict, and never answer from the counts you already sent.
168|
169|- Prove coverage by **set equality, not by totals**:
170|  `set(grid items for the period) == set(base media_id) == set(normalized captures media_id)`, printed as
171|  a boolean, plus the two difference sets (`in the grid, not captured` and `captured, not in the grid`),
172|  which must both be empty. Equal totals hide a swap; equal sets do not.
173|- Explain every absence with **fill counts segmented by dimension**: per metric, count filled rows and
174|  split by own/collab and by media type. An absence landing exactly on one segment (profile-activity
175|  missing in every collaboration and in no owned post) is a panel rule, not a capture failure — say which
176|  one it is instead of leaving a blank the user will read as data loss.
177|- Reconcile against the **previous version of the base**: every row of the earlier window must still be
178|  present, and name the fields that improved — the earlier run's empty likes column now filled is the
179|  proof the new pass earned its keep. A *value* changing on the overlap means the parser changed, not that
180|  the post moved.
181|- Report the period as `N/N` only when the set equality holds. A post whose panel returns placeholders
182|  after a re-read is `N/N-1`, named, with its documented status — never rounded up to "complete".
183|
184|## References
185|
186|- See `references/field-mapping.md` for a compact mapping of common Instagram insight labels to spreadsheet columns and collection notes.
187|- See `references/insights-panel-parsing.md` for the full post-level panel layout, the parsing rules (header-vs-likes, the `Facebook` overwrite, placeholder rejection), a reusable snippet, and the provenance rules.
188|- See `references/insights-collection-playbook.md` for the verified per-post flow (empty SEO shell, "Ver insights" clicked via JS), the three coexisting JSON shapes, the grid-scroll audit, the **shortcode → `media_id` → date** recipe, and how to resume a month collected across several sittings.

191|- See `references/infinite-scroll-collection.md` and `references/post-level-insights-capture.md` for the persistent-scroll collector and the per-post capture/parse details.
192|- See `references/incremental-run-and-pipeline-copies.md` for extending a period that is already partly collected: window/boundary proofs, copying (never overwriting) the pipeline for a follow-up run, sweep-vs-previous-run overlap verification, and a coverage audit that spans both runs.
193|- See `references/archived-stories-capture.md` for the **stories** layer — a third measurement that belongs to neither layer above: quantity per month/day from the app's own `day_shells` payload (the archive grid is virtualised and under-counts), media + `viewer_count` from `reels_media`, and the full per-story insight panel via the `PolarisMediaInsightsBaseSurfaceQuery` GraphQL call (one `media_id` per request). Run `scripts/coletar_stories_arquivados.js` in the archive page instead of hand-writing the hooks.
194|- See `references/account-level-insights-panel.md` for the account-level layer: the insights and ranked-content URLs with their query parameters, the metrics each view exposes, the DOM extraction recipe, a verified read (02/10/2026) with its reconciliation arithmetic, and the storage/reporting rules that keep the two layers from being conflated.

{"content": "1|# Prova de completude — como parar de desconfiar das capturas
2|
3|Regra que este documento existe para sustentar:
4|
5|> **Nenhum dado desta skill entra na camada canônica sem um veredito `COMPLETO` emitido por
6|> `scripts/verificar_completude.py`.**
7|
8|A dúvida "será que pegou tudo?" não se resolve olhando o resultado — ele *parece* completo
9|mesmo quando não está. Resolve-se com um artefato que cruza fontes independentes e **falha
10|alto** quando discordam.
11|
12|## O que deu errado em 02/10/2026 (para não repetir)
13|
14|Uma varredura de DOM em `/archive/stories/` devolveu 184 ids e *parecia* o mês inteiro. O
15|mês tinha 272 stories. Pior: a coleta de insights foi feita a partir dessa grade, então
16|cobriu só os dias que ela expunha (≥ 11/09) — **121 de 272 (44%), com 0% de cobertura em
17|sete dias** — e ninguém percebeu, porque os 121 registros estavam certos e consistentes.
18|
19|Três armadilhas que produziram isso:
20|
21|1. **Lista virtualizada.** A grade só materializa no DOM a janela visível. Rolar até o fim
22|   não garante nada: o recorte depende do tamanho da janela e do momento.
23|2. **Offset aplicado duas vezes.** O `timestamp` do `day_shells` é um carimbo de início de
24|   dia (`…T00:01:40Z`). Subtrair o offset de BRT e ler campos UTC joga **todo bucket um dia
25|   para trás**: descartou o bucket de 01/09 (3 stories) e puxou o de 01/10 (1 story) para
26|   dentro. As duas fontes "concordavam" porque o mesmo fuso errado foi aplicado nas duas.
27|3. **Fonte única.** Expectativa e inventário vinham do mesmo lugar, então concordar não
28|   provava nada.
29|
30|## O mecanismo: três fontes, cruzadas
31|
32|| Papel | Endpoint | O que prova |
33||---|---|---|
34|| EXPECTATIVA | `GET /api/v1/archive/reel/day_shells/` | `media_count` oficial por dia — **a plataforma manda** |
35|| INVENTÁRIO | `POST /api/v1/feed/reels_media/` (1 por bucket) | devolve exatamente `media_count` mídias daquele dia |
36|| CONTEÚDO | `POST /api/graphql` `PolarisMediaInsightsBaseSurfaceQuery` | 1 registro por mídia, com métricas reais |
37|
38|O verificador nunca reusa a fonte da coleta para se auto-validar. Ele compara as três.
39|
40|### Checks (todos fatais, exceto o último)
41|
42|| Check | O que exige |
43||---|---|
44|| `ESPERATIVA_POR_DIA` | para cada dia do mês, `media_count` == nº de mídias daquele dia |
45|| `SEM_BURACO` | total de ids únicos == soma de `media_count` |
46|| `SEM_DUPLICATA` | nº de entradas == nº de ids únicos |
47|| `MIDIA_UTILIZAVEL` | toda mídia tem `pk`, `taken_at` e URL de imagem ou vídeo |
48|| `INSIGHTS_EXATOS` | conjunto de ids com insights == conjunto de ids do inventário |
49|| `INSIGHTS_COM_CONTEUDO` | nenhum registro vazio ou com erro |
50|| `MEDIA_ID_COERENTE` | `media_id` decodificado bate com o `taken_at` em 100% |
51|| `BORDA_DE_MES` | *(aviso)* reporta os buckets vizinhos e o que ficou fora do período |
52|
53|**O `--offset` tem que ser o mesmo `timezone_offset` da coleta.** O dia do bucket é o dia
54|**local** da conta, não o dia UTC. Com UTC, 8 stories de 12/09 apareciam como 13/09 e 5 de
55|29/09 como 30/09 — divergência falsa que faria o verificador reprovar uma coleta correta.
56|Verificador com offset errado é pior que nenhum: ele "prova" um erro inexistente e treina
57|você a ignorá-lo.
58|
59|## Fluxo padrão
60|
61|```
62|1. console do app (instagram.com logado):  cole scripts/coletar_stories_periodo.js
63|2. await __IG.periodo('2026-09')
64|3. __IG.baixar('day_shells_2026-09.json', __IG.saida.day_shells)
65|   __IG.baixar('midias_2026-09.json',     __IG.saida.midias)
66|   __IG.baixar('insights_2026-09.json',   __IG.saida.insights)
67|4. mover os três de Downloads/ para a pasta da coleta
68|5. python scripts/verificar_completude.py --periodo 2026-09 --dir <pasta>
69|   -> exit 0  = COMPLETO  -> pode publicar na camada canônica
70|   -> exit 2  = INCOMPLETO -> NÃO publicar; o relatório diz exatamente o que falta
71|```
72|
73|Saída: `VERIFICACAO-<periodo>.md` (tabela dia a dia + checks + sha256 das fontes) e
74|`VERIFICACAO-<periodo>.json` (manifesto legível por máquina).
75|
76|O manifesto é o selo: ele amarra o veredito aos **hashes** dos três arquivos. Se qualquer
77|arquivo mudar depois, o hash muda e o selo deixa de valer — republicar exige reverificar.
78|
79|Cole o selo na nota do período:
80|
81|```
82|Completude: COMPLETO em 2026-10-02T19:58:12+00:00 | 19 dias | 272 stories | 272 insights
83|Fontes: day_shells a1b2… | midias c3d4… | insights e5f6…  (sha256[:16])
84|```
85|
86|## Convenção de arquivos
87|
88|```
89|capturas/instagram/<conta>/<periodo>/
90|  day_shells_<periodo>.json    expectativa oficial (media_count por dia)
91|  midias_<periodo>.json        inventário (mídias por dia, com URLs)
92|  insights_<periodo>.json      conteúdo (métricas por mídia)
93|  VERIFICACAO-<periodo>.md     relatório legível
94|  VERIFICACAO-<periodo>.json   manifesto + hashes
95|```
96|
97|## Transferência de payload do navegador para o disco
98|
99|O sink HTTP local (`127.0.0.1:8765`) **não serve**: o CSP do Instagram bloqueia `fetch`
100|cross-origin (testado; `TypeError: Failed to fetch`). O canal que funciona é blob + download:
101|o Electron grava em `Downloads/` com nome `<uuid>.tmp`. Copie para a pasta da coleta — e
102|identifique o arquivo pelo **conteúdo**, não pelo mais recente (três exports seguidos no mesmo
103|minuto confundem a ordenação).
104|
105|## Armadilhas específicas dos endpoints
106|
107|- **`id` do bucket já vem prefixado**: `archiveDay:2159257767957412`. Envolver de novo
108|  devolve `{"reels":{},"reels_media":[]}` com **status 200** — falha silenciosa.
109|- **`day_shells` só responde no contexto do app**; `fetch` direto devolve 232 bytes de erro
110|  (`1357004`). Rode o coletor na página logada.
111|- **`BaseSurface` aceita UM `media_id` por chamada**; lote devolve
112|  `variable_value_out_of_range`.
113|- **`reels_media` traz `viewer_count: null`** para a maioria dos stories. A contagem de
114|  visualizações confiável vem do `BaseSurface` (`umapi_unified_total_content_views_count`).
115|- **Nunca imprima tokens** (csrftoken, `fb_dtsg`, `lsd`, `jazoest`): o coletor os lê da página
116|  em tempo de execução e eles não devem sair do navegador.", "total_lines": 116, "file_size": 5997, "truncated": false, "is_binary": false, "is_image": false}
